title: Warm Challah Bread Pudding
headnote: Comforting, custardy bread pudding made with sweet egg bread, warm cinnamon, and nutmeg, served warm with vanilla ice cream. “You can try adding some fruit such as cinnamon sugar apples or diced/poached pears for delicious seasonal variations.” — Bob Mitchell

quotes.text: You can try adding some fruit such as cinnamon sugar apples or diced/poached pears for delicious seasonal variations.
quotes.span: “You can try adding some fruit such as cinnamon sugar apples or diced/poached pears for delicious seasonal variations.” — Bob Mitchell

items.raw: 2 tablespoons (28 g) unsalted butter, plus more for the dish
5½ cups (about 200 g) challah or brioche, cut into cubes
1 teaspoon cinnamon and nutmeg, mixed — heavier on the cinnamon

steps.text: Heat the oven to 350°F. Butter a 4- to 6-cup baking dish.
In a small saucepan over low heat, warm the milk, butter, vanilla, sugar, and salt just until the butter melts. Let it cool slightly.
Fill the buttered dish with the cubed challah or brioche.
Whisk the beaten eggs into the cooled milk mixture until well combined. It must be cool enough that the eggs do not cook.
Pour the mixture evenly over the bread, pressing gently so the bread soaks up the custard.
Dust generously with the cinnamon and nutmeg, leaning heavier on the cinnamon.
Bake 30 to 45 minutes, until the custard is set but still slightly wobbly in the center and the top edges of the bread are golden brown.
Serve warm with a generous scoop of good vanilla ice cream.

notes.label: Doneness
notes.text: a knife slipped in near the center should come out moist but without liquid custard (about 160°F).

notes.label: Stale bread is better
notes.text: day-old challah soaks up the custard without going mushy. If the bread is fresh, dry the cubes on a sheet pan at 300°F for 10 to 15 minutes first.

notes.label: With fruit
notes.text: fold cinnamon-sugar apples or diced poached pears in with the bread, as Bob suggests.

notes.label: Bigger crowd
notes.text: the recipe doubles into a 9×13-inch dish; bake toward the longer end of the time.
